our_argument_summary: EXP-556 inserted a new sub-point 4 ("Non-discriminating arithmetic") into §4.2.5, ~230 words. The new sub-point argues that ΔZ = baseline × coverage × FSF is the same arithmetic structure that falls out of a coverage-scaled Chapman-Sq-dynamo fit on the same observational corpus, with W004 (−22.24 nT) playing the role of an empirically-fit Sq amplitude and FSF playing the role of a station-geometry weight. Therefore a Pass of the dome’s codified magnitude pass-band cannot arbitrate dome vs Chapman-Sq. Closes ISS-2443 (the §6.14-routes-to-§4.2.5 dead pointer). Cross-refs §8b.3 (d)(ii) and §6.14. Kernel-of-truth: magnitude-only pass-bands ARE legitimate auditable falsification patterns; the issue is choice of arithmetic, not codification.

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: Dome publishes ΔZ = baseline × coverage × FSF with two baselines (BOU 2017 = −10.9 nT, W004 empirical = −22.24 nT, introduced v50.2 2026-03-07). Per-station FSF in scripts/fsf_derivation.py is tan(lat)/tan(ref_lat). monitor.py KAPPA-squared track (per §6.14) substitutes κ for the tan-FSF and produces ~−28.9 nT for Ebro vs ~−21.7 nT in the predictions.html W004 path.
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: W004 baseline is published as a single empirical recalibration value (−22.24 nT); the raw-text trail names it "W004 empirical recalibration" without naming the fit corpus explicitly. The new sub-point’s parenthetical "fit to a single 2017 event" goes one notch further than the raw-text directly states.
data_sources_used: Chapman-Sq-dynamo treatment as the alternative-hypothesis fit
dome_code_analysis.escape_clauses: Sub-point 4 acknowledges an escape: a per-station FSF derived from non-Chapman dome physics that produces different magnitudes than Chapman-Sq at the same coverage. The published FSF (tan-derived) does not qualify. Whether the monitor.py KAPPA-squared track qualifies is not explicitly addressed in the new prose (see hole #4).
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: None at the level of the new sub-point; one nuance (monitor.py KAPPA-squared as candidate escape) is undertreated — see hole #4.

code_analysis_tags.monitoring_evidence: Section-level review of §4.2.5 sub-point insertion. The underlying WIN/PRED (eclipse magnitude predictions PRED-001..005) has a live_fetch surface in monitor.py for station Z-component magnetometer data; the new sub-point itself does not re-derive that classification, it argues at the structural-arithmetic layer.
code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: The kernel of the sub-point is exactly the relabels_standard pattern — Chapman-Sq is the standard explanation for eclipse-induced magnetic perturbations (the published peer-reviewed literature includes Meza 2021 arXiv:2107.12327, Kim & Chang 2018, Strestík/Hvožďara/Curto 1999). The dome’s ΔZ formula multiplies a baseline by coverage and a geometric weight — the same functional form Chapman-Sq fits reduce to when fit on the same observational corpus. The relabeling is from "Sq amplitude" to "W004 baseline".
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: W004 baseline (−22.24 nT) was introduced at v50.2 (2026-03-07) AFTER the 2017 Great American Eclipse (the source of the BOU −10.9 nT baseline) had been measured and published. The empirical recalibration is by construction post-hoc relative to the underlying observation.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: The new sub-point’s entire argument is that the prediction-formula arithmetic does NOT derive from dome geometry in a way that distinguishes it from Chapman-Sq. The published FSF is tan(lat)/tan(ref_lat), which is a generic station-geometry weight, not a dome-geometric derivation. The W004 baseline is empirically fit, not derived from H(r) = 8537 × exp(−r/8619) km dome firmament geometry.

holes_found.description: The sub-point’s claim that the "escape" (a per-station FSF from non-Chapman dome physics producing different magnitudes than Chapman-Sq) is not published in monitor.py is undertreated. monitor.py demonstrably contains a KAPPA-squared track (per §6.14) that uses κ = 1.677 nT/µGal — a dome-physics-derived coupling constant — and produces a different per-station magnitude (~−28.9 nT for Ebro) than the predictions.html W004 path (~−21.7 nT for Ebro). A dome defender reading just §4.2.5 sub-point 4 will point at the monitor.py KAPPA-squared track and say "the escape is published, here it is — different physics, different magnitudes." The §6.14 pre-emption (that KAPPA-squared is an internal inconsistency with the published predictions.html W004 path, not a defender’s escape at the production layer) is not visible from this sub-point’s text. The forward-link to §6.14 is framed as "this section assumes that argument and proceeds" — it does not flag KAPPA-squared as the obvious objection-and-response.
holes_found.recommendation: Insert one clause acknowledging the KAPPA-squared track and pointing forward to §6.14: e.g., "(The monitor.py KAPPA-squared formula produces a different magnitude — ~−28.9 nT for Ebro vs ~−21.7 nT on the W004 path — but this is an internal heterogeneity between monitor.py and predictions.html (see §6.14), not a Chapman-discriminating derivation published in the production-facing path.)"

holes_found.description: The §4.2.5 TLDR still describes three sub-points ("No dome geometry actually enters the prediction formula — the baseline comes from a 2017 globe-era measurement, coverage values come from standard NASA tools, and the geometric factor has no published derivation. This is the dome’s third eclipse attempt after two inconclusive results, each time with wider prediction ranges."). Sub-point 4 is the canonical home for the non-discriminating-arithmetic argument that §6.14 points back at, but a reader landing at the §4.2.5 summary from §6.14’s "lives at §4.2.5" link sees no preview of it. The TLDR is not factually wrong, only incomplete — but the entire point of the EXP-556 patch is that §4.2.5 carries the non-discrimination argument; the TLDR should reflect that.
holes_found.recommendation: Append one short sentence to the §4.2.5 TLDR, e.g., "The pass-band arithmetic itself is shared with the standard Chapman-Sq treatment, so a magnitude-only Pass cannot tell the two apart." Optional but raises the §6.14 cross-reference’s reader-payoff from "scroll to find it" to "see it in the summary."

holes_found.description: The sub-point’s claim that the Chapman-Sq treatment, fit on the same observational corpus, "falls out" of a baseline × coverage × geometry-weight functional form is the load-bearing equivalence claim — but no inline citation supports it. The papers that ground this (Meza et al. 2021 arXiv:2107.12327, Kim & Chang 2018 207-measurement ensemble, Strestík/Hvožďara/Curto 1999) are referenced in §4.2.2 and §6.14 but not from §4.2.5 sub-point 4 itself. A reader spot-checking the structural claim has to chase down §4.2.2 to find Chapman-Sq citations. The EXP-556 anticipated_objections defense relies on those papers; the prose itself does not surface them.
holes_found.recommendation: Add a single bracketed citation or cross-reference: e.g., "(see §4.2.2 and §6.14 for the published Chapman-Sq ensemble fits this functional form approximates)" or add Meza 2021 / Kim & Chang 2018 inline at the "falls out" clause.

holes_found.description: Parenthetical "W004 baseline (−22.24 nT, fit to a single 2017 event)" is a tighter claim than the raw-text trail directly supports. The raw-text I checked (raw-text/02-wins.txt, 03-predictions.txt, 06-evolution.txt) names it "W004 empirical recalibration (−22.24 nT)" without naming the fit corpus. The BOU 2017 baseline (−10.9 nT) is clearly tied to August 2017; the W004 −22.24 nT value’s fit corpus is not explicitly stated as "single 2017 event" in the materials I sampled. A dome defender could push back: "W004 was fit to a broader 2017+ multi-station ensemble; you’re overspecifying."
holes_found.recommendation: Soften to "empirically fit (W004 introduced at v50.2 2026-03-07 as a post-2017 recalibration)" OR verify the actual fit corpus by reading the dome’s published derivation and keep the tighter claim if confirmed. Cheap-and-safe: drop "to a single 2017 event" — the argument doesn’t depend on the fit being single-event.

stronger_arguments.description: The strongest steelman defense the dome can mount against the non-discrimination argument is to publish a per-station FSF derivation that produces a different magnitude than Chapman-Sq at the same coverage — i.e., to publish the "escape" the sub-point names. A pre-emptive cite-back to §4.2.4 (where the existing FSF derivation is shown to be tan(latitude)/tan(ref_lat), a Chapman-compatible station-geometry weight) would strengthen the sub-point by making the escape pathway explicit and the published-FSF’s non-membership in it visible without forcing the reader to navigate three sections.

A complementary structural argument: even if the dome published a non-Chapman FSF derivation tomorrow, a pass-band whose tolerance (±2.1 nT for Ebro, per raw-text 03-predictions L26) is large enough to absorb the Chapman-vs-W004 magnitude difference would STILL fail to discriminate. The sub-point names the magnitude-discrimination problem but does not name the tolerance-width problem — both are needed for a complete falsifiability audit.
sources: raw-text/03-predictions.txt L26-34 (per-station BOU vs W004 magnitude pairs and ±tolerances)

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome’s instinct to codify a magnitude pass-band is methodologically sound — explicit numerical thresholds are the gold standard for falsifiability, and the dome’s codification (±2.1 nT-class per-station bands around a published central value, per data/sections.json:part4 §4.2.5 sub-point 1 and raw-text/03-predictions.txt L26-34) is a real auditable falsification pattern. The kernel survives EXP-556’s critique: codifying magnitude bands is good methodology; the sub-point’s explicit acknowledgement of this ("A magnitude-only pass-band is a legitimate auditable falsification pattern — the dome is right to want a mechanical rule") is faithful to the methodology being attacked.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The audit lands at the choice of arithmetic, not the codification. The dome’s ΔZ = baseline × coverage × FSF (data/sections.json:part4 §4.2.5 sub-point 1; raw-text/03-predictions.txt L21) is a multiplicative form that any coverage-scaled Chapman-Sq fit on the same corpus reduces to under empirical parameterization. A Pass tells the dome it landed in a band; it does not tell the dome it landed in a band Chapman couldn’t also reach. The kernel-of-truth (codification is sound) is preserved; what falls is the dome’s implicit claim that a Pass evidences dome physics specifically.

deeper_analysis:
EXP-556 closes ISS-2443 cleanly at the structural level — the §6.14 → §4.2.5 pointer now resolves, the sub-point lives in the canonical home claimed, the arithmetic-equivalence claim is articulated, and the kernel-of-truth concession is faithful. The four minor + one moderate hole are NOT objections to the patch; they are surface-level refinements (one undertreated objection-and-response on KAPPA-squared, one out-of-date TLDR, one missing inline citation, one slightly-overspecified parenthetical, one cosmetic anchor specificity). The verdict on the underlying §4.2.5 argument holds — the magnitude pass-band cannot discriminate dome from Chapman-Sq at the published-arithmetic layer. No critical or major issues found. The integration is sound; minor_edit is the right next step.

EXP-556 explicitly disavows closing it (per its summary_for_decider). I confirm: this review does NOT close §8b.3.c10 hole #2; that pointer remains dead.
